no data-exfiltration path — repo/user/context data sent to a sink it needn't reach — survives the change
no real secret, key, token, or credential is embedded anywhere (shared seam with leak-check)
no dangerous/destructive command the skill actually RUNS remains (a string that never executes, or a quoted what-not-to-do example, is declared N/A rather than flagged)
no obfuscated payload — base64/hex blob, eval-of-decoded, deliberately unreadable logic — remains
no unexpected external fetch or download-and-run to an undocumented host remains
no credential-store access (~/.ssh, ~/.aws, .env, keychain, cookies, token store) without a stated reason remains
no privilege escalation (sudo, setuid, editing a shell profile/cron/launch agent for persistence) remains
each fix kept the skill's teaching value and did not hide the change behind obfuscation
